title: Open localization of an augmented closed-intersection row
statement: Let i:Z→X be a closed immersion and W_a→X a finite family of closed immersions factoring through Z. Suppose i and every W_a have quasi-compact complementary opens. For a ring sheaf A and any Row D i W A of [def-sfb-closed-intersection-augmented-row], and any open immersion g:Y→X, there is a Row D_prime for the pulled-back family and inverse-image coefficients, together with OpenCompatibility D g D_prime. This is the full specified unit-normalized BaseChange data, the unit and face equations, and the complex isomorphism with its projection equation. There is no affine, covering, or contraction assertion.

proof.text: Localize the pro-etale site at the open scheme. On a test object T over that open, both open restriction of a closed direct image and direct image of the restricted sheaf evaluate on T times_X the closed subscheme. The resulting sectionwise isomorphism is linear and natural. For inverse images use the unit-normalized composition comparison around the pullback square. The ring comparison is its specified ringComp comparison, and the module comparison sends the successive inverse-image unit sections to the unit section transported by the canonical pasting isomorphism. These give delta, normalized and beta of BaseChange. Transposing beta by the fixed closed adjunction gives delta followed by the closed counit, because its defining section map is that evaluation map; this proves mate. The pullbacks of finite products over X are the finite products over the new base. For the empty index use the pullback of Z instead. These identifications give comparison for every term, preserving the actual unit sections. Closed units are epimorphisms by 09AH; thus the unit equation uniquely determines each inclusion face, and the comparison preserves it. Non-inclusion faces are zero. For a nonempty family construct the new row from the signed-refinement theorem and the augmented-row bridge, using the base-changed hypotheses. For an empty family take E_Z in degree -1 and zero in all other degrees, with zero differential. Take finite products of the comparisons above. Pullback preserves these finite products, and comparison of the signed matrices gives a map of complexes and its inverse. Equivalently construct the base row from the same unit faces on the new base and use the product comparisons for its differentials. This gives rowIso, and composition with each product projection is exactly components. All constructions include degree -1 and empty products. No quasi-compactness of the open immersion, affine hypothesis, or covering hypothesis is used.

theorem closed_intersection_open_comparison {X Z : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ X)
    [IsClosedImmersion i] {m : ℕ} (W : Fin m → Over X)
    (hclosed : ∀ a, IsClosedImmersion (W a).hom)
    (hfactor : ∀ a, Nonempty (W a ⟶ Over.mk i))
    (hqc : ∃ U : X.Opens, Set.range U.ι = (Set.range i)ᶜ ∧ QuasiCompact U.ι)
    (hqcW : ∀ a, ∃ U : X.Opens,
      Set.range U.ι = (Set.range (W a).hom)ᶜ ∧ QuasiCompact U.ι)
    (A : Rings X) (D : Row i W A)
    {Y : Scheme.{u}} (g : Y ⟶ X) [IsOpenImmersion g] :
    ∃ D' : Row (pullback.fst g i) (finiteClosedPullbackFamily W g) (inverseRing g A),
      Nonempty (OpenCompatibility D g D')
